clue.text: Lack expression to be obvious

definitions.meaning: read literally, to ... is to do without speech, lacking any expression
something that goes without saying is so plain it needs no stating

explanation.surface: Someone tongue-tied is told that their silence speaks for itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a truth so self-evident that nobody needs to voice it.

clue.text: She'll be the cause of the problem — Czech female and her male crush

definitions.text: She'll be the cause of the problem

indicators.note: to crush things is to squash them out of shape, so these letters are pressed into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman from Prague and her boyfriend are blamed for some trouble, with a hint of romance in the crush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crush' looks like a noun for infatuation, but it is the anagram signal for CZECH, FEMALE, HER and M.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase, literally 'look for the woman', suggests a woman lies behind any trouble.

clue.text: Main malt whisky distiller picked up legally empowered US citizen

parts.note: main means grand, as in the grand or main entrance

indicators.note: something picked up is heard, so the words are judged by their sound rather than their spelling

parts.note: Jura is a single malt whisky distillery on the Scottish island of that name

explanation.surface: The chief distiller of a malt whisky is collected by somebody, perhaps for a court appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: Jura is a Hebridean island whose distillery makes a well-known single malt; 'picked up' applies to it alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an American grand jury has legal power to decide whether a case goes to trial.

clue.text: Humorists uncovered cracks through which you might see the world?

definitions.text: through which you might see the world?

indicators.note: something that cracks breaks apart, so the remaining letters are broken up and rearranged
with its covers taken off, the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Comedians' jokes are little gaps offering a glimpse of how the world works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips HUMORISTS to UMORIST, and 'cracks' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel for pleasure is the industry through which holidaymakers get to visit other countries.

clue.text: Government department beginning to catalogue current central points

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, a British government department

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of catalogue is used

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A ministry starts listing its key focuses, with the current priorities at the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Foci is the plural of focus, the points on which attention or activity is concentrated.

clue.text: Spare tyre limp — grease added for repair

indicators.note: something sent for repair is taken apart and put back together, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A floppy spare wheel gets some lubricant before being taken to the garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare tyre' looks like a car part, but it is slang for a roll of fat round the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is jocular slang for the paunch that many people develop in their forties and fifties.

clue.text: Group ethos extremely fresh, excitedly welcoming remote team

parts.note: Queen was a famous British rock group

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one set of letters receives another inside it
excited things move about wildly, so these letters are jumbled
the extremes of a word are its outer letters, here its first and last

parts.note: out means remote, as in an out-of-the-way place

explanation.surface: A band's spirit is wildly enthusiastic about a far-flung side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' jumbles the letters to OFTHESH before 'welcoming' takes the inner piece. Queen of the South is a football club in Dumfries, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen of the South is the name of a Scottish professional football club, so it is a sporting side.

clue.text: Goatish creature, one into ladies?

indicators.note: one thing going into another is placed inside it

parts.note: the ladies is a women's toilet, and loo is a British word for toilet
the thar or tahr is a wild Himalayan goat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lecherous fellow is called a goat, someone very keen on women.
explanation.walkthrough: Goatish also means lustful, so the whole clue describes a seducer while its parts build the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a womaniser, named after a seducer in an 18th-century play; goatish means lecherous.

clue.text: Horrid type of slip packed by old duchess on vacation?

indicators.note: something packed by another is wrapped up inside it
a word on vacation is emptied of its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: an IOU is a slip of paper acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: An elderly aristocrat on holiday has packed a nasty item of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' suggests a petticoat, but here it is a written note of debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repulsive, a close synonym of horrid.

clue.text: Note close friend's short, a tiny measure

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its last letter

parts.note: a crony is a close friend

explanation.surface: A message from a pal is brief, a modest offering.
explanation.definitionFit: A micron is a millionth of a metre, a unit for very small lengths.

clue.text: Animal control scarce in report

parts.note: to rein is to control, as with a horse's reins

indicators.note: a report is a spoken account, so a word is taken by its sound

parts.note: dear means expensive because scarce, as in times when food is dear

explanation.surface: A news story describes the control of a scarce creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The reindeer is an Arctic deer, a domesticated animal of northern regions.

clue.text: 'H-Houston! Half of it's broken, we have a problem'

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are rearranged
half of a word is one of its two halves, here the first four of eight letters

explanation.surface: A stammering astronaut radios mission control as half the spacecraft breaks up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of it's' takes HHOU from the eight letters H-HOUSTON, and 'broken' rearranges them. The surface echoes Apollo 13's famous 'Houston, we have a problem'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uh-oh is an exclamation of alarm uttered on realising that something has gone wrong.

clue.text: The very thing left by critical attack when the axe drops?

definitions.text: left by critical attack when the axe drops
definitions.meaning: a critical attack is a hatchet job; drop the hatchet, the axe, and just the word job is left

explanation.surface: A savage review leaves something perfect behind once redundancies fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the axe drops' suggests job cuts, but the axe is the hatchet in HATCHET JOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Just the job is a British idiom for something exactly suited to the purpose.

clue.text: Going off, coming down or moving out?

definitions.text: Going off, coming down or moving out?

parts.words: Going off, coming down or moving out
parts.note: each phrase hints at departure, travel or falling ill, the queasy state of someone on a journey

explanation.surface: Three ways of leaving a place are listed.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrases read as departures, but 'going off' and 'coming down' also mean being sick or falling ill, while 'moving' is the travelling that causes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Motion sickness strikes passengers in cars, boats or planes, making them feel nauseous on journeys.

clue.text: Exceptionally cold and definitively negative

definitions.meaning: ... temperatures are below freezing, so very cold
a number below zero is by definition negative

explanation.surface: A weather report and a firm refusal are described together.
explanation.definitionFit: Below zero describes both freezing weather and any value less than nought on a scale.

clue.text: Mischievous nibble before meal's announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken aloud, so the words are judged by sound

parts.note: to gnaw is to nibble, and tea is a light evening meal in Britain, so GNAW comes before TEA

explanation.surface: A child sneaks a snack before dinner is called, being naughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Naughty describes badly behaved, impish conduct, especially in children.

clue.text: Swiss-German painter finally taken with English Times, an absorbing paper

parts.note: Paul Klee was a Swiss-born German painter

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is the one taken

parts.note: x is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: An artist is pictured with an English newspaper, absorbed in its pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' looks like 'engrossing', but it means soaking up liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Kleenex is a brand of tissue, a soft paper that soaks up moisture.

clue.text: By shop's entrance, father catches sick on back of expensive shoe

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter
the entrance to a word is its first letter
something that catches another holds it inside

parts.note: padre is a title for a priest, addressed as father
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Outside a boutique, a dad falls ill after seeing the price of shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a canvas shoe with a rope sole.

clue.text: Look for line expunged in glossy

indicators.note: something expunged is erased, so a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: sleek means smooth and glossy

explanation.surface: Someone searches for a deleted line in a shiny magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek something is to try to find it.

clue.text: Stiff vigil ending in very famous gardens surrounded by water

indicators.note: what is surrounded by another sits inside it

parts.note: a lake is a body of water

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Kew Gardens in London are famous botanical gardens

explanation.surface: A rigid vigil is kept at a renowned garden bordered by a moat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' is slang for a corpse. A lykewake is the old northern British watch kept over a body before burial.
explanation.definitionFit: A lykewake is a night watch over a corpse, so a vigil for a stiff.

clue.text: Side with everybody unknown

parts.note: all means everybody
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Someone joins forces with everyone, though nobody knows who.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally with someone is to join their side as a supporter.

clue.text: Bowie number succeeded in the future, 'Tom' having faded out?

parts.note: S is a genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

indicators.note: a name that fades out disappears, so those letters are removed

parts.note: tomorrow means the future
taken as written, the name being removed

explanation.surface: A David Bowie song hits the charts later, Major Tom having vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' recalls Major Tom of Bowie's Space Oddity, misleading towards that song.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow was a 1960s song that David Bowie covered as a hit single in 1973.

clue.text: Cutting deal, regularly handle hard stuff

indicators.note: a word cutting another splits it open and sits inside
regularly means taking every other letter of the word

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: Someone agrees a trade and routinely deals with spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard stuff' suggests strong drink, but it is the hard coating on teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is the hardest substance in the body, coating the teeth; it is also a hard glaze.

clue.text: After leaving Turkey, incisive head of state charms

indicators.note: letters leaving a word are taken out of it

parts.note: trenchant means incisive and keen
TR is the international code for Turkey

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sharp-witted leader wins people over after departing Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to delight or bewitch, so it charms.
